properties.name: Asking for gaps returns the design's own blind spots — the user is never the detector
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-07, and he named the point himself so it is quoted rather than paraphrased: "the bigger point I'm trying to make is not can you render some view and whether you do it accurately/honestly or not — it is that when I type /gaps, does reflow2 automatically find all these gaps/issues."

So honest rendering is NOT the requirement. A renderer that confesses is necessary and is already built. The requirement is that the FINDING is automatic: `/gaps` must surface the design's own blind spots without a human thinking to look for them.

WHAT detect_gaps DOES FIND, so the shortfall is not overstated: unsatisfied requirements, unallocated and unrealized and unverified capabilities, failing verifications, unreleased components, missing interface halves, status contradictions, duplicates, surprising couplings. Every one of those is a MISSING HALF OF SOMETHING THAT EXISTS. That is the shape it is good at.

WHAT IT DID NOT FIND, all measured on reflow2's own design on 2026-08-07, and every one of them found by a human querying by hand:
1. 6 Components sit in no subsystem, and `hierarchy_issues` returns 0.
2. `evaluate_allocation` reports modularity 1.0 from `total_internal: 1, total_external: 0` — a perfect score over ONE dependency, while the graph holds 171 DEPENDS_ON edges — and `graph_report` prints it as "Allocation health".
3. 30 of 60 edge types have ZERO instances. Nothing reports this. Among them `DECOMPOSES`, the edge for the recursive decomposition this project was built around.
4. 8 of 29 node types have zero instances, including `Actor`, `Flow` and `QualityGate` — so three viewpoints render empty and nothing says why.
5. Two node names contain HTML entities (`<`, `>`), i.e. escaped display text stored as design content.
6. Four whole UAF domains have no vocabulary at all (personnel, states, information, materiel) — which detect_gaps structurally cannot ask, because it reasons about instances and this is a question about the schema.

THE ASYMMETRY THIS NAMES: detect_gaps finds the missing half of something that was begun. It cannot find something that was NEVER BEGUN. A type with no instances, an edge type never drawn, a decomposition one level deep and a metric computed over one data point all look identical to a design that simply has no problem there. This is the same shape `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` already records for unsurfaced_gaps, where "clean" and "never scanned" are one answer, and the same shape `coverage_report` exists to fix for ARTIFACTS — there is no equivalent for vocabulary or structure.

THE PRECEDENT, and it is exact: `chg:orphan-decision-degree-zero` records this happening once already — "Found 2026-08-01 by running check-health and detect-and-ask on reflow2's own design, GETTING A CLEAN BILL FROM EVERY DETECTOR — detect_defects 0, hierarchy_issues 0, dimension_drifts 0, propose_heal 0 operations — and then counting zero-degree nodes by hand". One detector was added for that one case. The general principle was never made a requirement, so the next instance had to be found by hand again, which is what happened today.

ONE CONCRETE LEAD, because it is cheaper than it looks: `tools/render_views.py` already computes a CONFESSION LIST — everything a viewpoint needed and could not find — and it currently catches things detect_gaps does not, including every ChangeEvent pinned to no epoch and a real contradiction where `epoch:v0240-planned` and `epoch:v0250-planned` disagree between their PRECEDES edge and their sequence numbers. Two independent gap-finding mechanisms exist, the richer one is not wired into the loop, and `docs/viewpoints.md` already says "a confession list is a work list".

THE STANDING TRAP THIS MUST NOT FALL INTO, quoted from the catalogue's own rule 4: a detector that reaches zero findings by only asking questions the graph can already answer has been tuned to the instrument. Satisfying this requirement by adding checks that happen to pass is the failure mode, not the fix.

RELATED INTENT ALREADY IN THE GRAPH, so this is not read as unprecedented: `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` already states that the USER must never be the trigger — for skills. This is the same principle for findings.
